historical_stage_notes: Published AoS 52(4), 2024, pp. 1741–1773, 33 PDF pages. Source URL and hash match local manifest. No replacement download or web source was used.

Main text ends on page 25 at "The latter seems to be also a promising avenue for future research." Appendix heading begins at y=205.598; saved clip ends at y=204.59. Appendix content was not read. The PDF bookmark alone was insufficient to establish the endpoint because the conclusion continues onto that page.
Actual small-cap Theorem headings are 1 on page 8, 2 on page 11, 3–4 on page 16, 5 on page 17, 6–7 on page 18. Every full statement ends on its starting page.

Theorem 1 is nonasymptotic and uses empirical weighted norms, Algorithm 1 iterates, the penalized loss and the level-set radius R. Its max contains 1/[2R^2(1+q0)^2] minus 1, with the minus outside the fraction. R=0 leaves an undefined displayed reciprocal; preserve as a source issue.

Theorem 2 permits phi>0 to depend on dimension and approach zero. Theorem 3 requires it bounded away from zero. Do not merge these conditions or replace the sum error in Theorem 2 with the max error of Theorem 3.
Theorem 4 is pointwise at a fixed interior x_j and has three separate bandwidth bounds in (3.11). Theorem 5 is uniform over j and x_j in the closed interval and assumes (1+s1^2)nh^3->0.

Theorem 6 assumes only A1, A2, A4, A5 and A7. Its second branch adds both a regularity condition on true Theta_jk and a constraint on candidate Xi_jk in (3.7); this changes the optimization problem used for that branch. Preserve q in [0,1], including the sparsity-count convention at q=0.
Theorem 7 assumes q in (0,1], alpha in (0,1), beta>0 and a density-ratio decay bound after a permutation. It bounds both row and column summaries. No A assumptions occur in its printed statement.
Page 4 defines the additive model, population centering and function spaces; page 5 defines empirical centering. Population and empirical function representatives need separate treatment.

The normalizer c_h(u) is chosen by integration over the evaluation variable x, not over u. Its claimed bound 1<=c_h<=2 and the interior equality use kernel/small-bandwidth conventions that require source-scope review.

Joint density p-hat and marginal p-hat_j have exact marginalization due to the normalized kernel. Division by empirical densities in projection/marginal regression requires a domain convention on zero-density events.
The source uses the same norm symbol for a single function and for a tuple, with sum of squared component norms for the latter; do not confuse the sum-space norm with the tuple-space norm.

Section 2 uses off-diagonal uncentered empirical conditional-density kernels. Section 3 explicitly replaces them by centered kernels p-hat_jk/p-hat_j minus p-hat_k, while reusing the symbol Pi-hat. These are distinct local definitions even if they agree on centered inputs.

The operator identity is represented with Dirac delta on diagonal blocks, despite earlier kernel definitions using ordinary functions. Preserve this source convention separately rather than treating a Dirac distribution as a bounded kernel.

Algorithm 1 updates coordinates sequentially inside each sweep; it is not a simultaneous/Jacobi update. The printed unchanged-coordinate line omits hats. The positive-part threshold expression is undefined literally at a zero residual norm; record the usual zero-output convention as implicit, not as original text.
S is based on the population weighted norm; Sn uses the empirical norm. Equality is conditional on density-ratio bounds, not automatic by definition.

A6 is a conditional subexponential mgf bound over a finite interval of the transform parameter, not a sub-Gaussian condition for all real parameters. Response variance need not be uniformly bounded as d grows.
The paper defines stochastic lesssim as a bound by a fixed absolute constant with probability tending to one, which is stronger than generic O_P. Preserve its precise convention.

The compatibility constant uses expected smoothed density p^h, a cone on S, componentwise p_j^h centering, and a nonzero denominator. Its fixed argument is 6 sqrt(c_r,U/c_r,L), where ratio constants are defined in main-text (2.18); do not consult the cited supplementary lemma.
Page 15 states that I+Pi has eigenvalues in [0,1] and assumes invertibility. Preserve the assertion as source content with a separate issue, without relying on it as a verified mathematical fact.
A7 differentiates delta-tilde_jk as a function of u_j; Theorem 6 differentiates the kernel in its second coordinate x_k. Preserve the two different derivatives.

Gamma depends on |S| and a diverging sequence a_n through (3.6). The optimization objective is a sum of kernel sup norms, whereas its feasibility constraint uses the row mixed norm (3.5). Do not replace these with a generic operator norm.
Theorem 7 c_q(alpha,beta) must be read visually at high resolution before transcription; inspect the square-root extent in the first denominator rather than trusting extracted text.
The normal-limit display (3.12), confidence interval (3.13) and test (3.14) follow Theorem 5 but are not labeled Theorem. Do not add them to the inventory.

The statement that fLasso-SBF selects f-hat_j=0 for all j in S on page 12 appears inconsistent with S being the significant set. Do not use it to alter S or invent a theorem; record only if needed for source context.

Proposition 1 is excluded from the theorem inventory. Its conditions must not be imported merely to prove compatibility; a named constant or definition can still be preserved from main-text prose without using the proposition as an assumption.

Source extraction now contains D1 additive model, D2 function spaces, D3 normalized kernel, D4 marginal/joint density estimates, D5 loss/centering, D6 marginal regression, D7 pairwise density estimate, D8 projection, D9 scalar norm, D10 penalized estimator, D11 generic integral operators, D12 uncentered empirical operator, D13 penalty subgradient, D14 row/residual maps, D15 Algorithm 1, D16 true/empirical active sets, D17–D22 assumptions A1–A6, D23 expected-density marginalization and D24 compatibility constant. These local IDs are retained for continuation.

D18 describes only the population pair-density condition and does not depend on the empirical pair-density estimator D7. Population density notation needs auxiliary resolution, not an artificial estimator dependency.
